title: Could Doctor Doom's Time Machine Actually Work?

scenes.voiceover: Doctor Doom's time machine breaks one law of physics. And secretly obeys another.
scenes.visualConcept: A glowing time-vortex spiral pulling inward — ominous, cinematic.
scenes.backgroundPrompt: A swirling glowing time vortex in deep space, purple and gold.

scenes.voiceover: Time travel is not science fiction. Einstein's own equations allow a closed timelike curve — a path that loops back into the past. A mathematician found one on paper in nineteen forty-nine.
scenes.visualConcept: A looping ribbon of spacetime folding back on itself.
scenes.backgroundPrompt: A ribbon of spacetime curving into a closed loop, glowing grid.

scenes.voiceover: The catch isn't the law. It's the fuel. To hold that loop open, you'd need exotic matter with negative energy. And we've only ever made the faintest whisper of it.
scenes.visualConcept: A wormhole throat straining to stay open, energy draining.
scenes.backgroundPrompt: A wormhole throat held open by glowing exotic energy, unstable.

scenes.voiceover: So here's the verdict. The time loop is real physics. The machine that powers it is still, for now, pure magic.
scenes.visualConcept: Split screen: a clean equation vs a collapsing machine.
scenes.backgroundPrompt: Einstein field equations glowing beside a collapsing sci-fi machine.

scenes.voiceover: The full breakdown of the physics is on the channel.
scenes.visualConcept: Vortex pulls back to the opening spiral — loops to the hook.
scenes.backgroundPrompt: The time vortex spiral again, inviting.
